M1.reason: Silhouette overlap is 0.988 to 0.99 in every view, and the outlines match by eye: the octagonal body, the sloped top and the strap loop sit where the original's do. No part sticks out beyond the original's outline. The ragged strap edges in the front-left and front-right angles are surface faults, charged to M3 and M8.

M2.reason: Size is 34.6 x 26.3 x 6.8 against the original's 34.6 x 26.4 x 6.8, off by 0.4% at most on any axis.

M3.reason: Present and right in place: the body, the red cross and FIRST AID lettering, the screen with red and green lamps, the side dials in the left and right views, and the strap loop. But the strap is lumpy and broken (front-right, back-right) and the body has wedge-shaped gaps (back, front-right, back-left), so the strap and body faces are not the original's shape. The top panel's grey inset on the left is hard to match against the original, so I could not confirm it.

M4.reason: Measured mean colour difference is 10 (CIE76), under 15, with per-view values from 7 to 13.9. The white body, the dark strap and the screen panel read as the same colours and materials in every view. The strap's lighter patches in the reproduction's front view are within the same colour family.

M5.reason: The red cross, the FIRST AID lettering on top, the red arrow markings on the sides and corners and the red arrow on the top edge are all in their places, at a similar sharpness, in the top, side and angle views. The panel's screen, lights and dials are also present with the same markings.

M6.reason: Side by side, the reproduction reads as the same medkit at a glance, but the ragged strap and dark wedges on the sides in the back, front-right and back-left views would give it away at a closer look. A player would not take it for the original without a second look.

M7.reason: The control panel and first-aid cross face the front in both, the strap hangs the same way, and the object sits upright on its origin as the original does in the front and below views.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes with no errors and the triangle count (156) is within twice the original's (99). But the wedge-shaped gaps in the body's sides and the broken strap edges look like open or missing faces, so the mesh is not closed there.
